title: The Last Toast
hook: A wedding reception. Four hundred guests. One glass that should never have been poured.
contentNotes: A death by poisoning at a family celebration (no graphic detail).
Grief, debt and gambling are discussed.
All people and businesses are fictional.
briefing:
**Saturday, 13 June 2026.** Four hundred guests in wine and emerald filled The Glasshouse in Lekki for the wedding of **Simisola Bankole** and **Femi Daramola**. At 19:41 the bride's father, **Chief Adewale Bankole (64)**, raised a glass to his daughter. At 19:52 he collapsed beside the cake. He was dead by 20:40.

Chief Bankole never drank alcohol: doctor's orders. Tonight he drank champagne. By morning the lab had found a heart drug in his blood that no doctor had ever prescribed him.

Someone made sure he would drink. Read everything. Trust nobody. When you are sure, name the killer, say how it was done and why, and pin the three pieces of evidence that prove it.

You have three accusations. After that, the case goes cold.

evidence.title: Police incident report
evidence.source: Lagos State Police Command · Maroko Division · Insp. A. Okoro

body.markdown:
**Incident:** Sudden death at a wedding reception, The Glasshouse, Admiralty Way, Lekki Phase 1.
**Reported:** 19:55, Saturday 13 June 2026, by Mrs Folake Bankole via 112.

**Chief Adewale Bankole (64)**, father of the bride and chairman of Bankole Homes Ltd, collapsed at the high table at 19:52, a few minutes after the toast. Dr Ngozi Eze, a guest and his doctor, came back into the hall at 19:58 and began resuscitation. He was taken to Lagoon Crest Hospital and pronounced dead at 20:40.

First officers arrived at 20:15 and recorded a **suspected heart attack** in a known heart patient. The toxicology result (item 2) changed that.

Notes for the investigation:

- About 400 guests. The bride's family wore **wine** aso-ebi; the groom's family wore **emerald**.
- At 21:10 officers bagged everything at seat 1 of the high table: a brass cup of zobo and an empty champagne flute.
- The planners' room (Room B, beside the kitchen) was sealed at 21:00. Nobody has been in since.
- Statements were taken between 22:30 and 00:40.

evidence.title: Post-mortem and toxicology summary
evidence.source: Lagos State Forensic Pathology Unit · Dr K. Fashola

body.markdown:
**Cause of death:** cardiac arrest caused by **digoxin poisoning**. The level in his blood was about ten times the safe maximum.

Digoxin is a prescription heart medicine, sold as small tablets. It was **not** among the deceased's medicines (metformin, amlodipine and low-dose aspirin, per his doctor).

**Timing:** with a dose this large and his heart history, the drug was most likely swallowed **between 18:50 and 19:45**.

**Stomach contents:** jollof rice, small chops, zobo (hibiscus drink) and a small amount of champagne.

His smartwatch recorded a slow, irregular pulse from 19:47 (see his phone, item 15).

evidence.title: Statement: Folake Bankole
evidence.source: Interview by Insp. A. Okoro

lines.text: Adewale and I were married for twenty-two years. Simi is his daughter from his first marriage, but she is my daughter too.
His heart was weak. Since his operation he took no alcohol at all, only zobo. The caterers were told.
When the lights went off for the first dance, I went down with my husband to spray Simi and Femi. We walked back to the table together when the lights came up.
I wore our family's wine lace, with a gold gele. Mama Tinuke Fabrics made all our aso-ebi.
At the toast, Kola shouted that Daddy must drink with us. He laughed and drank. I thought the waiters had brought that glass.
His lawyer was coming on Monday about a new will. I don't know what was in it. Ask Kayode why he was shouting at his father this evening.

timestamps.label: Folake says she was on the dance floor with Chief

evidence.title: Statement: Kayode Bankole
evidence.source: Interview by Insp. A. Okoro

lines.text: I'm the first son. I run the Bankole Homes site office in Ajah.
My father and I did not argue today. We were fine.
At about seven-twenty I took a Chapman from the drinks station. For myself.
When the lights went out I was on the dance floor spraying my sister until the lights came back.
Ask Tunde about the deposits. My father was going to go through every file on Monday.
Dr Eze gave him all his medicine. If anyone knows about heart drugs, it's her.

timestamps.label: Kayode says he was on the dance floor

evidence.title: Statement: Dr Ngozi Eze
evidence.source: Interview by Insp. A. Okoro

lines.text: I have been Chief Bankole's doctor for eleven years, and a friend of the family.
He had heart surgery in 2024. His medicines were metformin, amlodipine and aspirin. I never prescribed him digoxin. He didn't need it.
At 18:47 my hospital called. A patient was crashing. I left the hall at once and drove to Lagoon Crest.
Mrs Bankole called me at 19:53. I came straight back and got here a little before eight.
I told the staff that nobody should touch his place at the table. The planner wanted the glasses cleared. I said no.
Yes, he and I disagreed about the hospital board. That is a matter for the board, not the police.

timestamps.label: Dr Eze says she left for the hospital
Dr Eze says she was back in the hall

evidence.title: Statement: Tunde Alabi
evidence.source: Interview by Insp. A. Okoro

lines.text: Adewale and I built Bankole Homes together over twenty years. I'm the finance director.
We have had one land case in twenty years, LD/1187/2019, and we won it. Our papers are always clean.
I sat at the high table from seven o'clock until the toast. I didn't leave my seat.
The Monday meeting was routine. He liked to look at the deposits every quarter.
I didn't touch his glass. I was at the other end of the table.
Kayode owes money to people you don't want to owe money to. Ask him.

evidence.title: Lab report: the high-table glasses
evidence.source: Police forensic laboratory, Alagbon · ref FL/0613/26

body.markdown:
- **Gold-rimmed flute, seat 1:** champagne residue. **Digoxin: yes, a large amount.**
- **Brass cup, seat 1:** zobo. Digoxin: no.
- **11 plain flutes, seats 2–12:** champagne. Digoxin: no.
- **3 opened toast bottles from the bar:** champagne. Digoxin: no.

**Fingerprints on the gold-rimmed flute:** Chief Bankole's only. Earlier smudging suggests it was handled with a cloth or gloves before he picked it up.

**The glass itself:** not a Bukka & Bites or Glasshouse glass. Maker's mark on the base: *Lumière, sold as a set of two*.

evidence.title: Search of the planners' room (Room B)
evidence.source: Police search · 13 June, 22:15

body.markdown:
Room B was sealed at 21:00. Found:

- Two staff bags labelled *Ese* and *Musa*, with their own clothes inside.
- One black Gold Petal uniform shirt on a hanger labelled *Ronke*: **unworn, still pressed**.
- An empty dress bag from Mama Tinuke Fabrics.
- A gift box made for **two** gold-rimmed champagne flutes, maker's mark *Lumière*. One flute is in the box. **The other slot is empty.**
- The foil and cork from a bottle of Moët numbered **#24**.
- In a make-up bag: an amber pill bottle, **empty**. Label: *DIGOXIN 250 microgram tablets · for: J. AJAYI · Kingsway Pharmacy, Yaba · dispensed 08/02/2022.*
- A teaspoon with traces of white powder (sent to the lab).

Assistant Musa Bala: "Ronke kept the key. She opened the room for us when we needed our bags."

evidence.title: Court record: Suit LD/1187/2019
evidence.source: High Court of Lagos State, Ikeja · registry extract

body.markdown:
**Suit LD/1187/2019 · Joseph Ajayi v. Bankole Homes Ltd and Adewale Bankole**

**Claim:** that the defendants took over the claimant's family land at Plot 9, Abijo, Ajah, using a sale agreement the claimant says he never signed.

**Witnesses for the claimant:** Mr Joseph Ajayi; **Miss Ronke Ajayi**, daughter of the claimant, who told the court her father "never sold our land to anybody".

**Judgment (14 October 2021):** claim dismissed. The claimant's original documents could not be produced; the court accepted the defendants' sale agreement.

**Registry note (2022):** claimant deceased, 3 March 2022. No appeal filed. File closed.
